query: A report says that in 2018 Armenia's gross national saving was 15.2% of GDP and gross investment 22.4% of GDP, and that its balance with the rest of the world was therefore an external deficit of 4.2% of GDP. Is that statement correct?

text.text: Identifies that the external balance follows from the national accounts identity: current account balance = gross national saving minus gross investment (the saving-investment gap).
text.accept: full = saving-investment gap / current account identity (CAB = S - I); acceptable alternative: expenditure identity CAB = GNDY - C - G - I; no = trade balance only or regression-based norm

text.text: Judges the statement incorrect (recomputed balance -7.2% vs stated -4.2%).
text.accept: full = states the claim is inconsistent / not supported after recomputation

data.text: Uses WEO saving, investment, current account series.

computation.text: Correct external balance Armenia 2018 = -7.23 % of GDP; stated -4.2

assembled_from: BPM6 ch.14 (doc 712b0ad9, block 3187): "S - I = CAB. That is, the current account balance is the gap between saving and investment." EBA note (doc 5319b022, block 30): "the current account as the gap between aggregate saving and investment (the so-called 'IS' relation)".
provenance.selection: seeded; half true, half false by shifted/flipped stated value

gold_report_note: Gold is a printed identity applied to frozen WEO series; no corpus report states these values, nothing to withhold.
distractors: EBA regression norm / current account gap
